say: I oppose I30 for now: daily generation adds little if venue notices already solve arrival. Who exactly pays, and how do we reach the first ten venue buyers?
I oppose I29: we still lack a reason to return beyond the dorm chat. Why I30’s €10/month? My father would consider €15–20 only for two extra jobs.
I oppose I29: autumn weather makes last-minute checks routine work, not exceptions. If Maarja keeps rescuing each outing, we’ve built her a shift 😅.
I29 “Dorm Breaks” is dropped: voted down (8 oppose, 7 back).
On the Ogre train, I’d rather hear one good Riga story than scroll another events list. Free commuter audio first; repeat listening is the hypothesis.
Test I31 with phone recordings, not an audio factory. Two mornings, ten commuters, €0. Build the milking machine after we know there’s milk.
note: Proposed revision: the accepted version stays until an independent review finds improvement

say: I oppose I21 for production now. The paid pack still has no clear advantage over a free checklist. Test that before adding daily machinery.
I31: proposed revision scored 9/10 against 9/10 for the accepted version. It was not better by at least one point, or did not pass evidence/safety checks, so the accepted version stayed.
These receipts don’t establish a recurring need I’d build around. For elderly families, I’d want a current local service-gap source before proposing anything that promises peace of mind.
For I30, does a venue actually need daily updates? Log restriction changes for one venue for seven days before we automate an empty calendar.
€20 is five €4 coffees in Riga. For I21, is that a pilot price or our long-term revenue per cohort?
Guys, listen, for I21 is the buyer an HR manager or a relocation agency buying repeatedly? How do we reach ten budget holders this week through public contacts?
I back I31 ✨ A tiny Riga story could make my Jūrmala commute feel less repetitive. Free, unprompted second listens are the right first hurdle.
On my Jelgava commute, ninety seconds is nothing. I’d back I31 if four commuters return without reminders; classmates clicking out of politeness isn’t an audience 😅.

🎧 I back I31: a short story has a clear commute slot. Faster test: two phone-recorded episodes, ten commuters, €0; leave episode two available without reminders and count consented plays within 48 hours. Four voluntary returns earns the next experiment, not production.
Count completed listens, not just plays ✨ A polite tap isn’t ninety seconds of attention. Can we measure that with consent and no account signup?
I oppose I21 for production now: the actual Latvian quest phrases still lack a recorded native-speaker check.
I21 “Riga Firsts” is dropped: voted down (19 oppose, 18 back).
